body:
_Migrated from issue #1374, filed 2026-08-04._

Surfaced while investigating #1372.

## What happens

When **Enable NextGen Automatic Cover & Metadata Enforcement Service** is off, editing a book's metadata saves to the library and the web UI reports **"Metadata successfully updated"** — but the book files on disk are never touched. Download the book back and the change is not in it. Sync it to a reader and the reader shows the old data.

The only signal that this happened is a line in the *container log*:

```
[cover-metadata-enforcer] The CWA Automatic Metadata enforcement service is currently
disabled in the settings. Therefore the metadata changes for <title> won't be enforced.
This means that the changes made will appear in the Web UI, but not be stored in the
ebook files themselves.
```

A normal user never sees that. From the UI, the edit looks like it worked, so the natural conclusion is that metadata editing is broken — which is how #1372 was first read.

## Two gaps

1. **No feedback at the point of the edit.** The success flash says the update succeeded without qualification. It could say the library was updated but the book files were not, and link to the setting.
2. **The setting is classic-UI only.** `auto_metadata_enforcement` appears in `cps/templates/cwa_settings.html` and has no equivalent in the SPA (`grep` over `frontend/src` finds nothing). A user who lives in the new UI cannot see the toggle that explains the behaviour, let alone change it. Related to #584.

## Not a default-state problem

Verified that a fresh install has this **on**: building `cwa.db` from `scripts/cwa_schema.sql` alone and inserting a default row gives `auto_metadata_enforcement=1`. So this only bites instances where it has been turned off — but when it does, it is invisible.

## Suggested fix

Qualify the save confirmation when enforcement is off, and expose the toggle in the SPA. Neither changes the enforcement behaviour itself, which is a legitimate choice for users who do not want their files rewritten.
title: Metadata edits are a silent no-op when enforcement is off — no indication anywhere in the UI
